engagement_tradeoff.why: 'Active role' and 'world affairs' had no examples.
engagement_tradeoff.scope: Think about the long run, not one conflict. An active role means things like military alliances, bases abroad, foreign aid, and pressing other countries on trade and security.

allies_tradeoff.why: No examples of working with allies versus acting alone.
allies_tradeoff.scope: Think about trade, security and diplomacy: for example, sanctions, military action, tariffs and climate or trade agreements.

defense_spending.scope: Today it is roughly $900 billion to $1 trillion a year, more than the next several countries combined. “Somewhat” means about 5% to 10%; “a lot” means a quarter or more.

foreign_aid_level.scope: Economic, health and humanitarian aid, not military aid. It has usually been about 1% of the federal budget. “A lot” means half again or more; “somewhat” means about 10% to 20%.

human_rights_tradeoff.why: 'Press on human rights' had no examples.
human_rights_tradeoff.scope: Countries that jail critics or persecute minorities. Pressing could mean sanctions, cutting arms sales or limiting trade.
